extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Middlebury Bread Loaf Writers' Conference (emerging and published writers seeking workshops or financial aid)
extracted.subtask_description: Application and acceptance guidelines for the Middlebury Bread Loaf Writers' Conference, including eligibility, application process, financial aid rules, selection criteria, fees, and enrollment requirements for participant applicants in fiction, nonfiction, and poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application window and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are accepted between December 1, 2025 and March 15, 2026. The application deadline is March 15 by midnight EST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to apply early. Application deadline is firm as midnight EST on March 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application method and platform
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply to the conference by submitting an application online. We use Submittable, the online application program. Applicants who already have a Submittable account will be asked to login. Others will be prompted to set up a free account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification letters are sent via Submittable in late May. For financial assistance with the application fee, contact Bread Loaf staff. Apply via the provided Submittable link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee and waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a $25 application fee; an application fee waiver may be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For financial assistance with the application fee, applicants should contact Bread Loaf staff to inquire about waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant applicant profile / eligibility (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant applicants are writers with a range of experience who are in the early stages of their literary careers or ongoing learners of the literary arts interested in feedback on work-in-progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The workshops are designed to accommodate both published writers and those in the early stages of careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of qualification / desirable background
rubrics_metrics.description: Our admissions board seeks emerging writers whose work shows talent and literary promise as well as those who already have an established literary background including publications in magazines and periodicals and/or an MFA or additional literary or academic training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both unpublished emerging writers showing promise and those with publications or advanced training are considered; emphasis is on talent and promise in the submitted writing sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria: writing sample strength and benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance is based on the strength and promise of the writing sample and the admission board’s judgment that the applicant will benefit from attending the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary evaluated artifact is the writing sample; the board also assesses whether the applicant would gain from the conference (fit and potential for growth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial aid: merit-based policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Thanks to the generosity of Middlebury College and also many donors... Bread Loaf is pleased to be able to offer substantial financial aid for both published and unpublished writers. Financial aid is merit based; financial need has no bearing on decisions, except as noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial aid awards are given on the basis of merit. Need will not be a deciding factor except where specifically noted elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial aid usage and frequency limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial aid must be used in the year it is granted. A writer may receive financial aid only once in a particular genre, with the exception of the Bread Loaf Returning Participant Scholarship and the Bread Loaf Returning Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If awarded, aid applies only to that conference year and is not automatically transferable. Exceptions exist for named returning-scholarship/fellowship awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying across multiple genres / multiple applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers who work in more than one genre can submit an application in each genre, if they wish. Writers who would like to be considered for a spot as a Participant should they not receive financial aid must submit a separate Participant application in addition to the financial aid application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting separate, complete applications is required for separate-genre consideration or to be considered as a paying participant if the applicant also applied for financial aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance rates and historical selectivity note
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2025 conference, we accepted 20% of paying participant applicants and 3% of those who applied for financial aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These figures show relative selectivity and may inform applicants about competitiveness; they are historical for 2025 and not a guarantee for future years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and post-acceptance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification letters are sent via Submittable in late May. Writers who submit more than one application will receive a notification letter for each application submitted. At the time of acceptance, a confirmation form is required in order to reserve one’s place, and Participants must submit their top choices for workshop leader at that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted applicants must complete the confirmation form promptly to hold their spot, and indicate workshop-leader preferences as part of the enrollment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment minimum (full conference attendance)
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not enroll anyone for less than the full ten days of the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should plan to attend the entire ten-day conference if accepted; partial attendance is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be at least eighteen years of age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No applicants under 18 will be enrolled; ensure eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant fees and cost breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee to be a Participant is $4,440. This includes tuition ($2,920) and room and board ($1,520).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget planning should reflect the total Participant fee and its components. Financial aid or scholarships may offset costs if awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript and reading opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants receive guidance on their work during the workshops and are invited to read during the Blue Parlor reading series. Upon acceptance, more information about the Blue Parlor reading series will be provided, as well as details on how to submit an unpublished manuscript for workshop critique. The Manuscript Guidelines are similar to those followed during the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted participants should follow Manuscript Guidelines (available separately) when preparing materials for workshop critique and readings; guidance and submission instructions are provided after acceptance.
